title: Prairie Ridge Grain Marketing Contracts: Programme Catalogue — Entry Terms and Contract Size
content:
The catalogue below is the entry side of the Grain Marketing Contracts offered by Prairie Ridge Cooperative Association. It sets, for each marketing programme, the smallest and largest number of bushels a single contract may be written for, the one-off fee charged when the contract is countersigned, and the paperwork the programme requires of the member before a contract is opened.

## Entry terms by programme

| Programme | Smallest contract (bushels) | Largest contract (bushels) | Setup fee charged at countersigning (USD) | Master marketing agreement required | Grain desk credit review required | Completed crop years of membership required |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Spot Cash Delivery Ticket | 1 | 100000 | 0.00 | No | No | 0 |
| Forward Cash Sale Contract | 1000 | 250000 | 0.00 | Yes | No | 0 |
| Basis Fixed Contract | 5000 | 400000 | 40.00 | Yes | Yes | 1 |
| Hedge-to-Arrive Contract | 5000 | 500000 | 60.00 | Yes | Yes | 2 |
| Delayed Price Agreement | 1000 | 300000 | 25.00 | Yes | No | 1 |
| Minimum Price Contract | 5000 | 250000 | 85.00 | Yes | Yes | 2 |
| Managed Accumulator Program | 10000 | 600000 | 250.00 | Yes | Yes | 3 |

The smallest contract figure and the bushels a programme will admit at entry are one and the same number: a Basis Fixed Contract is not written for 4,999 bushels, and a Managed Accumulator Program is not written for 9,999. The setup fee is charged once, when the contract is countersigned, and is not charged again on an application that is never countersigned.

## The same terms read as conditions

Where a member asks what a programme will take, the three conditions are read in this order of fact: the bushels offered stand at or above the smallest contract the programme writes and at or below the largest; the master grain marketing agreement is on file where the programme's column says it is required; and the grain desk credit review stands recorded as complete where that column says it is required. The completed crop years of membership column is the length of standing the programme asks for before entry.

## Points of judgement

A member holding a Delayed Price Agreement for 1,000 bushels is inside that programme's smallest contract, since the boundary figure itself qualifies. A member offering 600,000 bushels on a Managed Accumulator Program is at the largest contract that programme writes, and the figure itself is admitted. The Spot Cash Delivery Ticket asks for neither agreement, nor credit review, nor completed crop years, and writes contracts from a single bushel.
